observation.visible_scene: Against a near-black background with a faint cool light gradient in the upper-right, a round frosted/textured glass vessel sits at the bottom center of the frame. The vessel is filled with a glossy deep red/magenta liquid whose surface shows a bright specular streak on the right. Resting in the center of that surface is a small dome-shaped bead of the same red liquid, carrying its own tiny highlight. The vessel rim, the liquid surface, and the background stay in fixed screen positions throughout.
visible_changes: The central liquid bead/dome is present already in the first frame and persists to the last; it does not appear from nothing.
Over the ~2.67 s excerpt the bead's dome profile changes only very subtly, relaxing/settling toward a slightly flatter, lower mound by the end (frame 1 vs frame 41).
The bright reflection streak on the liquid surface and the highlight on the bead remain essentially stable in position and shape.
No translation of the vessel or bead is observed; the apparent change is local deformation of the bead, not movement across the frame.
No camera pan, tilt, or zoom is evident; framing of the vessel and background is constant.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produced the bead (e.g., an earlier drip or splash) is not shown; the segment begins with it already formed.
Whether the bead eventually merges into the surface or holds its shape is beyond the last frame.
uncertain_details: The bead's shape change is small; it is unclear whether it reflects a real slow settling/oscillation or compression/encoding noise.
The exact material of the vessel and liquid cannot be confirmed from the images alone.
